text:
sasha: heads up — brought up model v2.1-int4 on staging and seeing weird locale regressions for CJK and Arabic outputs, esp hyphenation and diacritics. attaching quick examples below :confused:
ming: can you paste a minimal prompt + bad output?
sasha: minimal prompt: "Translate to zh: 'The quick brown fox — jumps over the lazy dog.'"
   v2.1-fp16 (gold): "敏捷的棕色狐狸跳过了懒狗。"
   v2.1-int4: "敏 捷 的 棕 色 狐 狸 - - 跳 过 了 懒 狗 。"
   noticed extra spaces between CJK chars and duplicated hyphens.
ming: oof, that spacing looks like tokenizer splitting codepoint-wise. did quant step change tokenizer config?
sasha: not intentionally. deploy-bot: deployed v2.1-int4 to staging at 2026-11-03T08:14Z (rollout id r-443).
quant-bot: int4 quantization completed for v2.1, riffed on per-channel symmetric qparams (report: s3://redwood-artifacts/quant/v2.1/int4/report.html). :gear:
eva: could be sentencepiece vs bpe merge table mismatch at runtime — if tokenizer.model swapped or model was packaged without merges it can emit single-char tokens. check artifact bundle.
sasha: checking bundle now; tokenizer.model present, size matches upstream, but tokenizer.json missing merges field. hmm.
ryan: also saw Arabic diacritics move around in another run — likely a normalization/NFKC step got dropped before decode. sample: prompt "Translate to ar: 'She bought co-op shares.'"
   v2.1-fp16: "اشترت حصة في التعاون."
   v2.1-int4: "اش ت ر ت ح ص ة في ال ت -عا ون ."
   diacritics split and random spaces; ordering occasionally wrong (rtl markers?).
eva: can you run tokenizer.tokenize on the sample and dump token ids + strings? maybe a simple mismatch between tokenizer library versions.
ming: running local reproduce now with docker image `redwood/runner:v2.1-int4-staging` — will post tokenization dump. command I use:
```
# repro script
docker run --rm redwood/runner:v2.1-int4-staging \ 
  python -c "from redwood import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer('tokenizer.model'); print(t.encode('她买了合作社股份。'))"
```
ming: dump below (ids length 22): [101, 234, ...] and decoded pieces show single-codepoint pieces for CJK.
sasha: that matches. suspect issue in our packaging step where we compress tokenizer json and lose `spacer_heuristic`/merge table used by newer tokenizer runtime.
ryan: alternative possibility: quant runtime's custom kernel rewritten decode path accidentally toggles byte-level normalization; see recent commit on runtime/decoder that touched `normalize_unicode=True` flag. might flip behavior for NFKC.
eva: next steps: 1) reproduce deterministically with a pinned tokenizer lib (tokenizers==0.14.1) 2) repro with fp16 model to confirm quant only or packaging 3) run small eval suite against zh/jp/ar sentences to get BLEU/chrF diff.
sasha: I ran a quick eval: 500 sen pairs zh testset -> fp16 chrF=0.552, int4 chrF=0.431 (drop -0.121). ar BLEU drop from 28.4 -> 17.9. attached eval logs snippet: `s3://redwood-evals/multilang/v2.1-int4/20261103-summary.csv`.
m ing: thanks — that's pretty big. can we roll back staging to fp16 while investigating? deploy-bot: rolling rollback to v2.1-fp16, id r-442, initiated by @sasha. :white_check_mark:
ryan: I'll bisect the packaging pipeline. likely candidate: tokenizer packer job that gzips tokenizer.json but doesn't preserve `merge_rules` key when zipped.
eva: also add tests in onboarding harness to assert tokenization invariants for CJK (no spaces between han/jp characters) and Arabic diacritic alignment. I can draft a small pytest.
sasha: sounds good. @ming please collect exact tokenizer file diffs between fp16 and int4 bundles and upload. tagging @ryan for kernel/deploy investigation. i'll update the ticket with repro snippets. :memo:
ming: uploading diffs to ticket #ML-1729 now. will run the pinned-tokenizer repro and post results in the thread.
sasha: thanks everyone — let's aim to have a root cause by EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
